report.source_text: Evolution was marked by deterioration of the hematological and renal state along with the occurrence of hemorrhagic symptoms such as echymosis and haematemesis. The patient died secondary of a lactic acidosis.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with concurrent Evans syndrome
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with 2 months of fatigue, dizziness, and acute renal failure. Initial laboratory evaluation revealed: acute kidney injury (creatinine 330 µmol/L, GFR 14 mL/min), anemia (hemoglobin 86 g/L with reticulocytosis 5.2%), thrombocytopenia (platelets 36×10^9/L), and hemolysis markers (LDH 451 UI/L, indirect bilirubin 49 mmol/L, total bilirubin 96 mmol/L). Physical examination showed conjunctival jaundice. Direct Coombs test was positive for warm IgG antibody, establishing Evans syndrome (autoimmune hemolytic anemia with immune thrombocytopenia). Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation electrophoresis demonstrated a monoclonal IgG kappa M-spike with total serum protein 113 g/L and gamma globulin spike 69 g/L; urinary M protein was 2 g/day. Bone marrow aspirate showed 78% plasma cell infiltration, meeting diagnostic criteria for multiple myeloma. Whole-body CT-scan revealed osteolytic lesions in vertebral bodies (C5, D4, L3, L4) and left iliac wing, confirming myeloma with bone involvement. The acute renal failure was attributed to myeloma cast nephropathy from heavy proteinuria. BTD chemotherapy (bortezomib-thalidomide-dexamethasone) and continuous corticosteroid therapy were rapidly initiated. Despite treatment, the clinical course deteriorated with worsening hematological and renal parameters, hemorrhagic complications (ecchymosis and hematemesis), and ultimately lactic acidosis leading to death.
